_meta.title: Commission structure — official fixed rates
_meta.provenance: Both tables were fetched and read in full by session 3c6cba43 on 2026-11-13 from Amazon's public Associates help centre. No rate below is paraphrased; each is the literal value in the published table.
_meta.correction: An earlier draft of this project stated the rate card was not publicly retrievable. That was true only of the /help/operating/schedule endpoint, which does redirect to sign-in. The same Standard Commission Income Statement IS published publicly at the help-node URL cited as SRC-18. See FLG-013, corrected.

onsite_tableA.caption: Table A — Onsite Commission Income (Direct Qualifying Purchases, excluding Creator Ads)
onsite_tableA.note: Onsite Content is publisher or influencer content used by Amazon inside the Amazon Site. The same category earns materially less Onsite than Standard — Kitchen is 1.25 % here against 4.50 % in Table 1. Onsite income covers only a Direct Qualifying Purchase: the same ASIN variant the customer linked to, so the whole-basket effect of Standard commissions does not apply.

analysis.caption: What the rate card actually implies for an AI-led content strategy

rows.finding: The rate is set by category, not by price or by how well the item sells
rows.evidence: Table 1 maps categories to fixed percentages of Qualifying Revenue
rows.action: Niche selection should be solved as a category-rate problem first; product quality affects conversion, not rate.

rows.finding: The default band (4.00 %) beats four named bands
rows.evidence: 'All Other Categories | 4.00 %' vs Televisions 2.00 %, PC 2.50 %, Grocery/Health 1.00 %, the 3.00 % mega-band
rows.action: Prefer niches that fall outside the named lists — the unlisted default is the second-highest broadly-available rate.

rows.evidence: Kitchen 4.50 % vs Home 3.00 %; both are common 'appliance-adjacent' classifications
rows.action: Do not assume a product's band from its topic. Resolve the browse node via GetBrowseNodes before writing.

rows.finding: Onsite Content pays a fraction of the Standard rate
rows.evidence: Kitchen 1.25 % (Table A) vs 4.50 % (Table 1); and Onsite covers only Direct Qualifying Purchases of the same ASIN variant
rows.action: Traffic driven from off-site to one's own pages and then to Amazon is the higher-value path; publishing on Amazon surfaces pays less and is separately restricted.

rows.finding: Zero-rate categories are absolute, not relative
rows.evidence: Gift cards, alcohol, wireless plans, restaurant delivery, Coach, vehicles — 0.00 %
rows.action: The candidate generator excludes these categories at scoring time, so no content is ever drafted for them.

rows.finding: Bounties decouple income from basket size
rows.evidence: $12.00 per Prime registration or purchase regardless of order value
rows.action: A Prime-signup intent page can out-earn a product page per click; the optimiser scores EPC, which captures this automatically.

rows.finding: Rate cannot be attached to the three submitted products
rows.evidence: Category/browse node unresolved because the identifiers do not resolve (FLG-004…008)
rows.action: Per-product commission cells remain blank; the Kitchen figure is quoted as a category reference only.
